policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Ketiv בהשדה writes the article after the preposition; qere בַשָּׂדֶה contracts it. Both mean 'in the field', which is exactly what ASV renders; no italic supply or textual note is mapped. Retain qere base fallback.

Ketiv ההמון carries an explicit article; qere הֲמוֹן is construct before יִשְׂרָאֵל. ASV 'all the multitude of Israel' is the same English for either; the only note (hebrew_gloss 'in it') concerns a different word. Retain qere base fallback.
Ketiv בהחפזם spells the infinitive with ה after the preposition; qere בְּחָפְזָם contracts. Both mean 'in their haste', which ASV renders without italics or a mapped note. Retain qere base fallback.
